doc.title: Eddie Miller and Pete Fountain Interview, 1970-01-09

chapter: Callers, Bourbon Street and big bands
title: WNOE caller on Leon Kelner and hurricane relief
summary: Eddie Deer recalls Leon Kelner's long tenure in the Blue Room and thanks Pete for Hurricane Camille relief.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: Yes, sir. Turn your radio off, will you please?
Turn it off. Now, a little. Hello.
Eddie Deer from WNOEFM. I'm listening to the program.
And just wondering, who is this, Doug?

Yeah, I didn't recognize your voice at first. I know everybody over there. I don't think I've met you. Talking about Leon Keller, it's been about 26 or 27 years in the Blue Room. Used to be around the Gulf Coast, Biloxi. You know, in between. You know, the four years.
I think he went at the Broadwater years ago. Years ago. Right.
Yeah, I'd seen him over there. I lived over there for a while. You're talking about Pete Fountain, too, on there, huh?

Yeah, he's there. I wanted to just mention, too, that, again, he doesn't expect any medals or any thanks, but for the beautiful contribution to the Gulf Coast victims of Hurricane Camille that he did so gracefully and wonderfully. And I've enjoyed your programs all the time, all the programs that you have. So I just wanted to mention that. I auditioned the radio. I was at Blue Room Cashier for five months at night, you know. And, of course, I knew Jack Delaney and Terry Andrews called up. I've known him for years and so forth and so on. So I know Leon and I still go there now and then and catch the new shows from time to time. So, again, congratulations to Eddie Miller, Pete, you, everybody on the program.
And Bob Middleton does a very fine job. Okay, Doug, thank you. I'll make it short.
Yes, sir. Thank you very much.
